final.paragraph:
This is an automated hazard-exposure briefing produced by Riprap from live and precomputed data sources. It is informational only and not a substitute for a professional risk assessment.

**In brief.**
This address is outside the 2012 Sandy inundation footprint [sandy_inundation], in FEMA flood zone X (an area of minimal flood hazard) on the 2007 effective map [fema_nfhl], and outside the modeled flooding in the DEP stormwater scenarios for current, 2050 and 2080 sea-level rise [dep_moderate_current][dep_moderate_2050][dep_extreme_2080]. 17 flood-related 311 complaints were filed within 200 m in the last 5 years [nyc311].

**Hazard Reader.**
This address sits outside the empirical 2012 Hurricane Sandy inundation footprint (NYC Open Data) [sandy_inundation]. This address sits in FEMA flood zone X (an area of minimal flood hazard), per NFHL FIRM panel 3604970203F, effective 2007 [fema_nfhl]. FEMA's preliminary flood map (PFIRM issued 2015-01-30, community 360497) places this address in zone X (an area of minimal flood hazard) [fema_pfirm]. A preliminary map is not the effective map and does not set flood insurance. NYC DEP stormwater scenarios at this address: current sea level with 2.13 in/hr of rain, outside the modeled flooding [dep_moderate_current]; 2050 sea-level rise with 2.13 in/hr, outside the modeled flooding [dep_moderate_2050]; 2080 sea-level rise with 3.66 in/hr, outside the modeled flooding [dep_extreme_2080]. No Hurricane Ida (Sept 2021) high-water marks were surveyed within 800 m of this address [ida_hwm]. Nearest USGS-surveyed mark: South of Bedford Ave., between north 12th St. and Lorimer Ave., in McCarren Park, Brooklyn (2396 m away) [ida_hwm]. Elevation 6.51 m; this point is higher than 66% of the ground within 200 m (the 66th percentile; a low percentile means a local low spot where water collects) [microtopo].

**Live Observer.**
2 FloodNet community sensors within 600 m have logged 6 above-curb flood events in the last 3 years, the most recent starting 2026-07-29 15:03 UTC [floodnet]. FloodNet's record showed no flood event under way at them when this was read (2026-10-02 12:29 UTC) [floodnet]. Peak depth recorded by the sensors in good working order: 96 mm (3.8 in) on 2026-07-18 [floodnet]. 17 NYC 311 flood-related complaints filed within 200 m of this location in the last 5 years: 7 catch basin, 5 sewer backup, 4 street flooding, 1 manhole overflow [nyc311].

**Asset Register.**
2 MTA subway entrances within 800 m of this address: 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 2 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [mta_entrance_exposure]. Inside the DEP extreme scenario (2080 sea-level rise), by station: Delancey St-Essex St (F M J Z) (754 m) [mta_entrance_exposure]. 6 flood-exposed NYCHA developments within 2000 m of this address (the register lists only developments found inside the 2012 Sandy extent or a DEP stormwater scenario, not every development): 4 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 2 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [nycha_development_exposure]. Inside the 2012 Sandy extent: BARUCH (420 m), WALD (797 m), LOWER EAST SIDE REHAB (GROUP 5) (1084 m), RIIS (1305 m) [nycha_development_exposure]. Outside the 2012 Sandy extent but within 50 m of its mapped edge (the outline is not exact to a building): BARUCH HOUSES ADDITION (337 m), TWO BRIDGES URA (SITE 7) (621 m), LA GUARDIA ADDITION (757 m), LOWER EAST SIDE II (984 m), RIIS II (1037 m), LOWER EAST SIDE III (1180 m), SMITH (1613 m) [nycha_development_exposure]. Inside the DEP extreme scenario (2080 sea-level rise): SEWARD PARK EXTENSION (642 m), FIRST HOUSES (1179 m) [nycha_development_exposure]. 4 flood-exposed NYC DOE schools within 1500 m of this address (the register lists only schools found inside the 2012 Sandy extent or a DEP stormwater scenario, not every school): 4 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 0 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [doe_school_exposure]. Inside the 2012 Sandy extent: Bard High School Early College (577 m), Girls Preparatory Charter School of New York (682 m), Brooklyn Navy Yard STEAM Center (1463 m), The Children's Workshop School (1499 m) [doe_school_exposure]. Outside the 2012 Sandy extent but within 50 m of its mapped edge (the outline is not exact to a building): P.S. 110 Florence Nightingale (215 m), P.S. 184m Shuang Wen (553 m), New Explorations into Science, Technology and Math High School (589 m), P.S. 034 Franklin D. Roosevelt (1390 m) [doe_school_exposure]. 7 hospitals within 3000 m of this address; of the nearest 5: 0 inside the 2012 Sandy inundation extent and 2 inside the DEP extreme stormwater scenario (2080 sea-level rise) [doh_hospital_exposure]. Inside the DEP extreme scenario (2080 sea-level rise): NYU Langone Orthopedic Hospital (2235 m), Brooklyn Hospital Center - Downtown Campus (2712 m) [doh_hospital_exposure].

prithvi_water.narrative: Experimental: a satellite model on Sentinel-2 scenes from 2021-09-02, the day after Hurricane Ida, compared with 2021-08-13, showed 0 m² of new surface water within 500 m of this address (89% of it observed); of 7 other heavy-rain events since 2017 with a clear pass over this place, it showed new water after 2 (2020-04-13, 2022-07-18). Limits: a satellite passes every few days and sees 10 to 20 m pixels, so street and basement flooding that drains within hours is invisible to it, and its training labels were the base model's own output for Hurricane Ida, not surveyed flooding; of 153 high-water marks USGS surveyed after Ida, it showed new water within 500 m of 17 (11%), no better than chance (14% of the land it saw lies that close to its new water). Rely on the surveyed and measured record (USGS high-water marks, FloodNet sensors) and NYC DEP's stormwater flood maps.

landcover.narrative: Experimental: a satellite land-cover model estimates that 67.8% of the ground within 500 m of this address is paved or built over and 30.9% is green (17.2% tree canopy), on Sentinel-2 scenes from 2026; no change between years is read from it, because its maps of different summers differ by more than two images of one summer do (between 2018 and 2024, 49 of 59 districts' paved shares differ by more than 2.0 points). Limits: it estimates the share of each 10 m satellite pixel that is canopy, grass, paving, roof, water or bare ground, learned from the city's 2017 six-inch map, so detail finer than about 30 m is blurred and a tree over a street counts as canopy; against the city's own 2021 six-inch map, on squares it never trained on, it read a typical district's paved share 1.7 points above the map's (at most 7.8 points off), and two images of one year differ by under 2.0 points in a district's paved share 19 times in 20 (2.7 in a neighbourhood's). Rely on NYC's own land cover maps (2017 and 2021, 6 inch) and building footprints for a survey.
